\begin{abstract}
Candidate restriction can reduce influence-maximization search costs, but evaluating its quality requires comparing two seed sets selected from finite samples. We vary the selection-world budget $W$ for both full-candidate and candidate-restricted greedy selection, separately from ranking precision, and evaluate spread on 10,000 independent worlds. Evidence comes from three external topologies, with four small contact graphs providing separate controls. On ca-GrQc, the mean pathwise relative incremental-spread difference for default PageRank-4k changes from $+5.61$\% to $-5.07$\% against the same-budget full reference. This sign reversal disappears in a post-hoc control that tightens PageRank tolerance. Budget-dependent seed changes persist, but set changes alone do not determine the direction or magnitude of independently estimated spread changes. Across the external networks, degree-based pools reproduce all 15 highest-budget reference trajectories at lower measured selection cost, whereas PageRank losses persist on the two directed networks. These findings distinguish selection-budget sensitivity from candidate-ranking sensitivity. Reporting both selection procedures, candidate-pool stability and independently evaluated spread makes the basis of a measured quality--cost trade-off explicit.

\begin{abstract}
Restricting seed candidates can reduce influence-maximization cost, but the resulting quality judgment depends on how both compared seed sets are computed. We separate the shared selection-world budget from candidate-ranking precision and assess selected seeds on 10,000 independent worlds. Three external networks provide the main comparison, with four small contact graphs supplying separate controls. On ca-GrQc, default PageRank-4k changes from a mean relative incremental-spread difference of $+5.61$\% to $-5.07$\% as the selection budget increases. A post-hoc tolerance control replaces two candidates and removes this mean sign reversal, while budget-dependent seed changes persist. Independent evaluation also distinguishes set instability from utility change: 16 of 40 historical reference sets change, with a mean spread increase of 0.01111 nodes across all pairs. At the highest external budget, 20-node degree pools reproduce all 15 reference trajectories at lower measured selection cost. PageRank losses remain on the directed networks. These results identify a precision-sensitive quality judgment and quantify when different seed outputs correspond to different spread, linking candidate compression to its measured utility and cost.

\item[(1)] \textbf{We identify how ranking precision alters an apparent budget effect.} We vary the selection budget for both full and restricted arms and use a post-hoc precision control to examine the resulting relative spread differences. On ca-GrQc, tightening PageRank tolerance exchanges two of 20 candidates and removes the default mean gain-to-loss reversal. This identifies a numerical dependence that a budget scan at default tolerance alone would miss.
\item[(2)] \textbf{We quantify independently estimated spread changes associated with reference-set changes.} Independent paired evaluation measures their direction, magnitude and conditional Monte Carlo uncertainty. In the historical comparison from $W=1280$ to $W=5120$, 16 of 40 reference sets change, while mean spread increases by 0.01111 nodes across all 40 network--path pairs. Individual changes include negative, positive and zero differences; the measurements separate seed-set instability from changes in estimated utility.
\item[(3)] \textbf{We identify which tested candidate pools preserve the reference while reducing selection cost.} At $W=1280$, Degree-4k uses 20 candidates to reproduce all 15 external reference trajectories at lower selection cost in this implementation. Default PageRank-4k reproduces none, and losses on CollegeMsg and wiki-Vote persist under tighter tolerance. These comparisons delimit the transfer of earlier contact-graph agreement and relate computational savings to independently evaluated utility.

\section{Conclusion}
Candidate-restriction quality depends on finite-world seed selection in both methods and on the ranking that defines the restricted pool. Increasing $W$ changes both selection procedures; independently evaluated relative differences therefore describe their joint response to the selection budget. On ca-GrQc, tightening PageRank tolerance removes the apparent budget-induced sign reversal, while budget-dependent seed changes remain. Separate reference-transition comparisons distinguish changes in seed membership from the direction and magnitude of estimated spread changes. Across the external sample, Degree-4k preserves the tested $W=1280$ trajectories at lower measured selection cost, whereas PageRank outcomes depend on precision, coverage and network context. Evaluation reports should distinguish the shared selection budget, the independent evaluation budget and candidate-pool construction, and report signed spread differences alongside scoped costs. These findings apply to the networks, propagation settings and implementations examined here.

\section{Conclusion}
The paired comparisons identify a ranking-precision dependence in a budget-based quality judgment and quantify the spread consequences of seed changes. On ca-GrQc, the default mean reversal disappears after the candidate pool changes under tighter tolerance; budget-dependent seed changes remain. Independent evaluation distinguishes these changes from their signed utility effects. On the external networks, degree pools preserve the highest-budget reference at lower selection cost, while PageRank illustrates losses and partial recovery through greater coverage. For the tested simulation settings, reporting candidate membership, both methods' selection budget, independent spread and scoped costs makes the quality of candidate compression assessable.

\begin{abstract}
候选限制能够降低影响力最大化的搜索成本，但评价其质量需要比较两个由有限采样选出的种子集合。本文同时改变全候选与候选受限贪心选择的选择世界预算 $W$，单独控制排名精度，并在 10,000 个独立世界上评估传播量。三张外部网络用于主要比较，四张小规模接触图提供单独的补充对照。在 ca-GrQc 上，默认 PageRank-4k 相对同预算全候选参照的逐路径相对增量传播差异，取跨路径均值后由 $+5.61$\% 转为 $-5.07$\%。这一符号反转在收紧 PageRank 容差的事后控制中消失。预算相关的种子变化仍然存在，但仅凭集合变化无法确定独立估计传播量变化的方向与大小。在外部网络上，基于度的候选池以更低的实测选择成本复现了最高测试预算下全部 15 条参照轨迹，两个有向网络上的 PageRank 损失则仍然存在。这些发现区分了选择预算敏感性与候选排名敏感性。同时报告两类选择过程、候选池稳定性和独立评估传播量，能够明确实测质量与成本权衡的依据。

\begin{abstract}
限制种子候选范围能够降低影响力最大化的计算成本，但对其质量的判断取决于参与比较的两个种子集合如何计算得到。本文分别控制两类方法共享的选择世界预算与候选排名精度，并在10,000个独立世界上评估已选种子。三张外部网络提供主要比较，四张小规模接触图提供单独对照。在ca-GrQc上，随着选择预算增加，默认PageRank-4k的平均相对增量传播差异由$+5.61$\%变为$-5.07$\%。事后容差控制替换两个候选节点后，这一平均符号反转消失，但预算相关的种子变化仍然存在。独立评估进一步区分了集合不稳定性与效用变化：40个历史参照集合中有16个改变，而全部配对的平均传播量增加0.01111个节点。在最高外部预算下，含20个节点的度候选池以更低的实测选择成本复现全部15条参照轨迹；有向网络上的PageRank损失仍然存在。这些结果识别了对精度敏感的质量判断，量化不同种子输出所对应的传播差异，并将候选压缩与其实际效用和计算代价联系起来。

\section{结论}
候选限制的质量取决于两类方法的有限世界种子选择，以及定义受限候选池的排名。增加 $W$ 会改变两类选择过程，因此，独立评估的相对差异描述了二者对选择预算的共同响应。在 ca-GrQc 上，收紧 PageRank 容差使表面上由预算引起的符号反转消失，但预算相关的种子变化仍然存在。单独的参照预算转移比较区分了种子成员变化与估计传播量变化的方向和大小。在外部网络样本中，Degree-4k 以更低的实测选择成本保持了已测试的 $W=1280$ 参照轨迹，而 PageRank 结果依赖精度、覆盖率与网络背景。评价报告应区分共享选择预算、独立评估预算与候选池构建，并同时报告有符号的传播差值和明确范围的计算成本。这些发现适用于本文考察的网络、传播设置与实现。
after:
\section{结论}
配对比较识别了预算相关质量判断对排名精度的依赖，并量化种子变化的传播后果。在ca-GrQc上，更严格容差改变候选池后，默认设置下的平均反转消失，但预算相关种子变化仍存在。独立评估将这些变化与其有符号效用差异区分开来。在外部网络上，度候选池以更低选择成本保持最高预算参照，而PageRank展示了传播损失及增加覆盖率后的部分恢复。对于已测试的模拟设置，同时报告候选成员、两类方法的选择预算、独立传播量与明确范围的成本，可以使候选压缩的质量得到具体评价。
